_note: Teardown/breakdown data for the Showroom's exploded view. Anchors in FITTED car space (~3.4 units long, grounded y=0, +X nose, +Y up, +Z left). `materials` are GLB material-name substrings matched first-match-wins in this part order; empty = not a mesh in this GLB → callout. The FL5 ships real engine (EngineA), brakes (Callipers), and wheel meshes. It's FWD like the FC3, so the un-modeled drivetrain + suspension use the procedural transaxle/suspension stand-ins (geometrically apt for a transverse FWD four). Copy grounded on data/cars/12-honda-civic-type-r.json; anchors from frontend/scripts/model_meshes.mjs.

parts.label: 2.0L K20C1 Turbo Engine
parts.summary: Honda's most powerful factory four — a 2.0-liter turbo making 315 hp, mounted transversely.
parts.detail: K20C1 2.0L turbo four making 315 hp and 310 lb-ft (FL5), Honda's most powerful factory four, mounted transversely and driving the front wheels.
parts.watch: The engine is tough, but Honda under-sized the cooling; sustained track use spikes oil temps and trips limp mode, and cold climates can see some oil dilution.

parts.label: Brembo 4-Piston Front Brakes
parts.summary: Brembo 4-piston front monoblocks on 350mm rotors — genuine track-capable stoppers.
parts.detail: Brembo 4-piston front monoblocks on 350mm rotors with 2-piston rears — strong enough for repeated hard lapping.
parts.watch: The hardware is up to it, but the factory pads and fluid fade under repeated hard lapping, so upgrade both before serious track days.

parts.label: 19" Matrix Wheels & Tires
parts.summary: Nineteen-inch matte wheels on wide, sticky rubber — the grip the LSD chassis is built to use.
parts.detail: Factory 19-inch wheels on 265/30R19 performance tires — the wide, grippy setup that feeds the helical LSD and the dual-axis-strut front end.
parts.watch: No real weak spot — just watch for curb and pothole wheel damage on the low-profile OEM tires.

parts.label: Interior & Driver's Cockpit
parts.summary: Red sport seats, a metal shifter, and the driver-first Type R cockpit.
parts.detail: Signature red bucket seats and red carpeting, a machined-alloy shift knob on the rifle-bolt six-speed, and a +R drive-mode cockpit with a digital cluster.
parts.watch: Bolster wear on hard-used cars; the infotainment is improved over the FK8 but still not class-leading.

parts.label: Lighting & Electronics
parts.summary: Full-LED lighting and the Type R's LogR data suite.
parts.detail: LED head and tail lamps plus Honda's LogR datalogger and performance monitor — the Type R's built-in track telemetry.
parts.watch: Generally robust; keep the head-unit software updated for the LogR and infotainment features.

parts.label: Body, Aero & Glass
parts.summary: A chassis 15% stiffer than the FK8, with a functional wing and diffuser — and the FWD 'Ring record.
parts.detail: Steel unibody 15% stiffer than the FK8, with more mature styling, a functional rear wing, wider track, and real underbody aero. Reclaimed the FWD Nürburgring lap record.
parts.watch: Solid structure; watch for rock chips and parking dings, and confirm no track-day contact on used examples.

parts.label: 6-Speed Manual & Helical LSD
parts.summary: A rifle-bolt six-speed — the only gearbox — with a helical LSD and rev-matching.
parts.detail: FWD via a rifle-bolt 6-speed manual (the only gearbox) with a helical limited-slip diff and automatic rev-matching. (Shown as a procedural stand-in — not a separate mesh in this model.)
parts.watch: Heavily tracked cars, notably the earlier FK8, can break 3rd/4th gear (reinforced gears exist); both gens have some rev-hang on upshifts.

parts.label: Dual-Axis Strut & Adaptive Dampers
parts.summary: A dual-axis front strut to kill torque steer, multi-link rear, and adaptive dampers.
parts.detail: Dual-axis strut front (to kill torque steer), multi-link rear, and adaptive dampers on a chassis 15% stiffer than the FK8 — widely called the best-handling Type R yet. (Procedural stand-in — not a separate mesh.)
parts.watch: No real weak spot; just watch for curb and pothole wheel damage on the low-profile OEM tires.
